messages:
Noah Li: Hey all, excited to be here! Quick onboarding snag: I set up the desk with two monitors and a KVM switch I had at home. Laptop sleeps fine on USB-C but when waking the left monitor (connected via the KVM -> dock -> DP) shows black and the headset (USB-C dongle) connected to the dock isn't recognized. Also the corp wifi cert never popped up during setup so SSO/VPN fails with 'no user certificate'. Anyone seen this pattern or should I open an IT ticket?

Zara (IT): Welcome Noah :wave: Sounds like a few layers: KVMs can interfere with EDID/HDCP passthrough; first check by connecting that left monitor directly to the dock (bypass KVM) to isolate. For the headset, try plugging into a different USB-C port on the dock or direct to the laptop. For the cert: did you run the onboarding script at https://onboard.redwood.example? If not, run it and watch for a certificate prompt. If you want I can open a ticket.

Noah Li: Thx Zara. I tried direct to dock (bypassed KVM) and the monitor comes up fine, so KVM is suspect. Headset still not recognized on dock but works when plugged straight to laptop. Ran the onboarding script and it completed but the VPN still errors: "AUTH_ERROR: no user certificate found for uid=noah.li". I'm remote in Portland so can't swap hardware in-person.

Zara (IT): Good isolation. For the headset, two quick things: 1) power-cycle the dock (unplug usb-c power, wait 15s), 2) check Device Manager / System Report to see if the USB descriptor changes when you plug the headset into the dock (this helps us see if it's a power/descriptor passthrough issue). For the cert, open certmgr.msc (Windows) or Keychain Access (macOS) and verify a user cert exists under Personal/Certificates with CN=noah.li. If it's missing, run the cert installer from the onboarding page again; if present but VPN still rejects it, paste the VPN log tail. I'll create a ticket to track the dock/KVM interaction and the cert issue since you're remote.

Noah Li: I'm on macOS Ventura (MBP 14 M2). In System Report > USB the headset doesn't appear when on the dock, but shows when plugged straight to laptop. I power-cycled the dock; no change. Keychain shows no cert with my name. I re-ran the mac cert installer, it asked for admin password, then showed "Installed user cert (noah.li)". VPN still fails with same error.

Zara (IT): Thanks. Two possibilities: 1) the installer wrote the cert to the System keychain instead of Login (we've seen that on Macs with custom profiles), 2) the VPN client needs the cert in the Login keychain and unlocked at login. Open Keychain Access -> select 'Login' -> see if the cert is there. If it's in 'System', export and re-import into Login or run the installer with the flag to target Login. I'll open IT-2476 to get identity team involved and to authorize a loaner powered USB hub + alternative dock in case the remote dock is flaky.

Logistics Bot: Ticket IT-2476 created by Zara (IT) for Noah Li 00 "KVM causes DP blank, dock USB-C audio passthrough missing, user cert not seen by VPN". Priority: P2. Action: identity team looped, loaner USB hub & alt dock to be shipped pending approval. ETA triage: 3 hours.

Maya (People Ops): Welcome Noah :tada: Sorry about the bumpy start. If shipping a dock works better than troubleshooting the KVM remotely we can expedite. Also note: if the KVM is company policy-incompatible, please hold onto it until we confirm replacement gear. I can approve a coworking stipend if the hardware delay impacts your onboarding.

Noah Li: Appreciate the help. Keychain had the cert in System but not Login  moved it to Login and VPN auth now succeeds. Headset still dead on the dock so I'll keep IT-2476 open for the loaner hub/dock and to confirm the KVM won't get in the way. Thanks zara and team! :thumbsup:
